subject: GK
text: Who is popularly known as the 'Iron Man of India'?
explanation: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel is called the Iron Man of India for his role in integrating over 560 princely states into the Indian Union.

subject: GK
text: Which is the largest country in the world by total land area?
explanation: Russia is the largest country, covering more than 17 million square kilometers, spanning across Eastern Europe and Northern Asia.

subject: GK
text: On which date is World Health Day celebrated globally every year?
explanation: World Health Day is celebrated on April 7 to mark the founding of the World Health Organization (WHO) in 1948.

subject: GK
text: What is the capital city of Japan?
explanation: Tokyo is the capital of Japan, functioning as the center of the Greater Tokyo Area, the most populous metropolitan area in the world.

subject: GK
text: Which inert gas is commonly filled in electric bulbs to prevent the oxidation of the tungsten filament?
explanation: Argon or Nitrogen is used because it does not react with the hot tungsten filament, increasing the bulb's lifespan.

subject: GK
text: Who was the first Indian sportsperson to win an individual Olympic gold medal?
explanation: Abhinav Bindra won gold in the 10m Air Rifle event at the Beijing 2008 Olympics, becoming India's first individual gold medalist.

subject: GK
text: Who was the primary founder of the Indian National Congress (INC) in 1885?
explanation: Allan Octavian Hume (A.O. Hume), a retired British civil servant, took the initiative to establish the INC to create a political platform for Indians.

subject: GK
text: What was the name of India's first research station established in Antarctica in 1983?
explanation: Dakshin Gangotri was the first Indian scientific research station in Antarctica, later decommissioned and replaced by Maitri and Bharati.

subject: GK
text: Which Indian state is the largest producer of Rice in the country?
explanation: West Bengal is the leading rice-producing state, accounting for over 13% of the nation's total rice cultivation.

subject: GK
text: Which constitutional amendment act reduced the voting age in India from 21 to 18 years?
explanation: The 61st Amendment Act (1989) amended Article 326 of the Constitution to reduce the voting age to 18 for Lok Sabha and Assembly elections.

subject: GK
text: Which high mountain pass connects Srinagar to Leh in the Ladakh region?
explanation: Zoji La Pass is a critical pass on National Highway 1, connecting the Kashmir Valley with Ladakh.

subject: GK
text: Where is the head office of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) located?
explanation: ISRO is headquartered in Bengaluru, Karnataka, managing the space exploration and satellite program of India.

subject: GK
text: Which is the largest gulf in the world by coastline and basin area?
explanation: The Gulf of Mexico is the largest gulf in the world, bounded by North America, Mexico, and Cuba.

subject: GK
text: Under which article of the Indian Constitution is the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) appointed by the President?
explanation: Article 148 provides for an independent office of the CAG of India, who acts as the guardian of the public purse.

subject: GK
text: Who was the last Governor-General of independent India, serving from 1948 to 1950?
explanation: C. Rajagopalachari was the first and last Indian Governor-General of independent India before the office was abolished in 1950.

subject: GK
text: Who was the key founder of the revolutionary 'Ghadar Party' in San Francisco, USA, in 1913?
explanation: Lala Har Dayal was the founding leader and secretary of the Ghadar Party, which sought to end British rule in India through armed revolution.

subject: GK
text: Which meridian is selected as the Standard Meridian of India, determining Indian Standard Time?
explanation: $82^\circ 30'\text{ East}$ longitude, passing through Mirzapur in Uttar Pradesh, is the Standard Meridian of India.

subject: GK
text: Which Indian state is the largest producer of Iron Ore in the country?
explanation: Odisha is the leading producer of iron ore, followed by Chhattisgarh and Karnataka, housing major high-grade hematite deposits.

subject: GK
text: What is the primary difference between a direct tax and an indirect tax?
explanation: Direct tax is levied directly on the income or wealth of a person (tax burden cannot be shifted); indirect tax is levied on goods and services (burden can be shifted to consumers).

options.text: Indirect tax is paid only by corporations; direct tax by retail citizens
Direct tax is paid directly on income/wealth; indirect tax is levied on goods/services and can be shifted to consumers
Direct tax is regulated by states; indirect tax by the central government alone
Direct tax applies only to cash transactions; indirect tax to electronic ones

subject: GK
text: In which city is the National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (NEERI) situated?
explanation: NEERI, a constituent laboratory of CSIR, is located in Nagpur, Maharashtra, focusing on environmental science and engineering research.

subject: GK
text: Who was the first Indian journalist/writer to win the prestigious Pulitzer Prize in 1937?
explanation: Gobind Behari Lal won the Pulitzer Prize for Journalism in 1937 for coverage of science, working as a science editor for Hearst newspapers.

subject: GK
text: Which British legislation proposed a federal system of government at the center and introduced provincial autonomy by abolishing dyarchy in provinces?
explanation: The Government of India Act 1935 introduced provincial autonomy, abolished provincial dyarchy, and planned a Federation of India (which never materialized).

subject: GK
text: How does a Solar Eclipse occur?
explanation: A solar eclipse occurs when the Moon passes directly between the Sun and the Earth, blocking solar rays and casting a shadow on the Earth.

options.text: The Earth comes between the Sun and the Moon
The Moon comes between the Sun and the Earth
The Sun comes between the Earth and the Moon
Venus aligns between Earth and Sun

subject: GK
text: In economics, what is the 'Gini Coefficient' used to measure?
explanation: The Gini Coefficient (or Gini Index) is a statistical measure of economic inequality, representing income or wealth distribution within a nation.

options.text: The rate of inflation in industrial sectors
The degree of income or wealth inequality within a population
The efficiency of commercial bank lending systems
The ratio of agricultural exports to imports

subject: GK
text: Which supersonic cruise missile is developed as a joint venture between the Defense Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) of India and NPOM of Russia?
explanation: BrahMos is a medium-range ramjet supersonic cruise missile, named after the Brahmaputra and Moskva rivers, capable of being launched from land, sea, sub-sea, or air.
